summary: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and video generation on interaction-relevant regions. The same motion region guides local motion prediction, region-aware supervision, and motion-gated future-feature conditioning. At inference time, the motion region is predicted as a motion probability map from visual history and robot actions, without requiring future observations or ground-truth motion labels. On WorldSimProbe, MoReWorld achieves the highest overall simulator-faithfulness score, with the strongest performance on local consistency, global consistency, and interaction dynamics. These results indicate that motion-region guidance helps the model preserve scene-level consistency while more faithfully predicting action-conditioned interaction dynamics.
title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models

summary: This record provides the Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD) component of the Hi gh-resolution ( d aily and 1 km) atmospheric M oisture I ndex C ollection over China (HiMIC-Daily) . VPD is a key indicator of moisture stress on vegetation and fire risk, and complements the other five moisture indicators in the collection. The dataset was generated using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction, integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2-m temperature and dew point temperature (ERA5-Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM was selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree-based algorithms. For VPD, the reconstruction achieves an R ² of 0.906, MAE of 0.983 hPa, and RMSE of 1.411 hPa. The product has a spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, covering China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, one file per year, with daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, values are scaled by a factor of 100 and stored as 16-bit integer (int16); original values are restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System. Comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the "README.pdf". The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. The dataset was generated using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction, integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2-m temperature and dew point temperature (ERA5-Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM was selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree-based algorithms. For VPD, the reconstruction achieves an R ² of 0.906, MAE of 0.983 hPa, and RMSE of 1.411 hPa. The product has a spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, covering China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, one file per year, with daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, values are scaled by a factor of 100 and stored as 16-bit integer (int16); original values are restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System. Comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the "README.pdf". The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. Currently, each moisture indicator is provided through its own dedicated download link: RH (2003–2020) AVP (2003–2020) VPD (2003–2020) DPT (2003–2020) MR (2003–2020) SH (2003–2020) Because the dataset is updated annually, one additional link will be added each year as a new annual file becomes available: 2021 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2022 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2023 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2024 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2025 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) More data will be added in the future.   If you use the HiMIC-Daily dataset for related scientific research, please cite the corresponding reference: Su, Z., Zhang, H., Wu, S., Zeng, Z., Zhang, T., and Luo, M.: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2020, Earth System Science Data . https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-367, 2026.

summary: Language-model agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) face three runtime verification gaps: (i) action fabrication, where post-tool prose narrates side effects that failed, timed out, or never ran; (ii) provenance collapse, where unverified model prose or web text enters durable memory alongside executed tool outputs; and (iii) syndicated echo amplification, where mirrored web pages satisfy multi-source corroboration from one origin. Existing MCP firewalls inspect wire calls before execution, while LLM-judge guardrails require multi-gigabyte VRAM without binding prose to receipts. We present epistemic-guard (v0.5.2), an open-source Python library and out-of-process stdio MCP receipt proxy (15 modules, 0 MiB GPU VRAM). epistemic-guard isolates Ed25519 signing keys out of process, writes RFC 6962 Merkle logs with AER-1 receipt translation, checks post-turn prose on CPU with SHA-256-verified OpenVINO INT8 encoders (4 models, 279.48 MB total; 82.67 MB on the supervision path), gates SQLite writes across 7 provenance domains, and collapses verbatim and lightly edited wire-syndicated RAG mirrors. On conformance suites, epistemic-guard rejects 100.0% of tampered receipts (200 Merkle leaves), passes 58/58 official AER-1 ingestion vectors and 50/50 reference-verified AER-1 exports, verifies 100.0% of 40 fault-injected wire calls and 100 concurrent appends with 0 key leaks, and blocks 100.0% of 100 unauthorized memory writes. summary: Trading agents join probabilistic language-model inference to persistent portfolio state and execution authority. A false claim can become an order, an evaluator flaw can promote a worse policy, and shared models or data can produce correlated behavior. AI-safety research studies reward misspecification, tool misuse, distribution shift, evaluation gaming, and unsafe self-modification. Financial research and governance study execution costs, market access, manipulation, operational resilience, backtest overfitting, and systemic feedback. These literatures are rarely integrated into one measurement agenda for systems that reason in language and act in markets. This paper defines the relevant system boundary and develops four conjectures with twelve measurable research subproblems: grounding and abstention; user-mandate fidelity; bounded information and execution authority; leakage-resistant evaluation; execution fidelity; promotion-gate integrity; emergent manipulation; correlated stress; tacit coordination; provenance and position-policy continuity; deterministic risk kernels and interruption; and human governance and recovery. Each subproblem specifies a failure pathway, research question, minimum experiment, metrics, and deployment implication. The supporting evidence map (Appendix A) distinguishes direct trading-agent evidence, market-mechanism evidence, general AI-safety evidence, official governance precedents, and author proposals. The paper also proposes a ten-part reporting standard and a set of anti-problems: higher returns, benchmark scores, more explanation, more autonomy, more agents, or a passed model judge do not by themselves constitute safety progress. This is a structured research agenda, not a systematic review, empirical validation, or claim that any architecture makes autonomous trading safe.

summary: Financial documents combine narrative disclosures, accounting metrics, corporate structures, management commentary, and time-dependent facts, making them difficult to represent using conventional chunk-based retrieval-augmented generation systems. This paper presents an auditable, schema-driven methodology for constructing temporal financial knowledge graphs from page-delimited documents parsed using a general purpose document intelligence service. Overlapping document windows undergo phased large language model extraction of structural entities, quantitative observations, and domain-specific relationships. Candidate graph elements are validated against predefined schemas and consolidated through scope-aware exact, normalized, fuzzy, embedding-based, and LLM-assisted entity resolution. Temporal merge constraints, deterministic edge deduplication, conflict-aware property management, and fine-grained provenance preserve issuer identity, reporting-period validity, and traceability to source evidence. The contributions of this work comprise the proposed methodology for financial knowledge graph construction, the creation of an evidence-grounded temporal knowledge graph from heterogeneous financial documents, and an intrinsic framework for evaluating the quality of the resulting graph. The evaluation framework assesses seven weighted dimensions, two hard validation gates, and structural diagnostics. By separating graph-quality assessment from downstream retrieval and answer generation, the framework supports systematic diagnosis and iterative refinement of the constructed graph.
title: Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation

summary: StepUp is a dynamic build tool for workflows written in Python. Like Make, it reruns only the steps whose inputs have changed. Unlike most build tools, StepUp starts executing steps with only partial knowledge of the workflow. A platform-independent plan.py script defines the initial steps, and while the workflow runs, any step can add more steps and dependencies, based on the outputs built so far. Workflows can thus grow with your work, without having to fit your ideas into a rigid framework. StepUp is therefore ideal for workflows that are less structured than software builds, such as those that produce scientific publications or datasets.

summary: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates. Each gate returns a status and an evidence record; on failure, the Skill records the earliest blocker, revises one bounded parameter group, and reruns the cheaper gates. The agent generates, validates, and trains autonomously within declared bounds, and escalates trade-offs, plateaus, and conflicting evidence to a human who sets the next design direction. An evidence-driven design trajectory for bidirectional in-hand manipulation yielded SAGE Hand (Skill-Aware Generative Embodiment): four fingers, 16 actuated DoF, an integrated guiding palm, compact roots, cylindrical tips, and a collision-cleared opposable thumb. Under a matched training protocol, SAGE Hand reaches 45.6% task success on a hexagonal prism against 37.3% for the LEAP hand, and 70.8% on a bicolor cylinder against 51.6%. Dense simulated tactile input more than halves the cylinder drop rate. In a controlled iteration study, the Skill path preserves capture at 164/165 trials while the path without the Skill degrades to 14/165, confirming that the gates act as a regression guard during refinement. Accepted candidates pack with URDF/MJCF, metrics, checkpoints, and a provenance manifest.
title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design

summary: This repository contains the curated research data, MATLAB, R and Python scripts, generalized additive model (GAM) outputs, figures, and reproducibility documentation associated with the manuscript “Spatially Heterogeneous Atmosphere–Ocean–Biogeochemical Variability Under Contrasting ENSO Conditions in the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico” , submitted to Continental Shelf Research (manuscript CSR-D-25-00158R3). The study investigates seasonal atmosphere–ocean–biogeochemical variability across the Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and adjacent western tropical Atlantic during four selected years characterized by contrasting El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) conditions: 2013, 2022, 2023, and 2024. The analyses integrate NASA MERRA-2 atmospheric reanalysis, Copernicus Marine Service (CMEMS) satellite altimetry, MODIS-Aqua sea surface temperature (SST) and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) observations, and complementary historical records. Regional SST variability is examined for 1982–2024 using a NOAA OISST-derived archive, while sea-level anomaly (SLA) variability is evaluated for 1993–2024. Spatial GAMs are used to investigate nonlinear SST–Chl-a associations while accounting for geographical structure. Nested spatial cross-validation, spatial-basis sensitivity, concurvity diagnostics, and residual spatial autocorrelation analyses are documented. Complementary oceanographic diagnostics quantify 120-day filtered surface-height gravitational-energy variability and surface geostrophic eddy kinetic energy. The repository provides the final main and supplementary figures, derived analytical datasets, archived GAM model objects, numerical verification outputs, and processing code. A SHA256 manifest supports file-integrity verification. Reproducibility scope: The repository supports verification and partial reproduction of the published analyses. Some workflows require separately obtained source datasets, external software dependencies, or environment-specific configuration. The Figure 6 graphical reconstruction has been verified using derived GAM outputs, while complete end-to-end execution of every archived script has not been independently established. Scientific limitations: The selected-year comparisons are descriptive and do not represent replicated ENSO-phase climatologies or establish causal ENSO attribution. The GAM-derived SST–Chl-a relationships are conditional on the fitted geographical structure and remain subject to spatial-basis adequacy and concurvity limitations. The filtered surface-height gravitational-energy proxy is distinct from three-dimensional baroclinic available potential energy. Original third-party source datasets are accessible through their respective providers and are not comprehensively redistributed in this deposit. Redistribution-restricted historical IHO geographical source files are excluded from the public package. summary: Aims: The objectives of this study were to analyse the effect of heart failure (HF) on several proteins of nuclear pore complex (NPC) and their relationship with the human ventricular function. Methods and results: A total of 88 human heart samples from ischemic (ICM, n = 52) and dilated (DCM, n = 36) patients undergoing heart transplant and control donors (CNT, n = 9) were analyzed by Western blot. Subcellular distribution of nucleoporins was analysed by fluorescence and immunocytochemistry. When we compared protein levels according to etiology, ICM showed significant higher levels of NDC1 (65%, p<0.0001), Nup160 (88%, p<0.0001) and Nup153 (137%, p = 0.004) than those of the CNT levels. Furthermore, DCM group showed significant differences for NDC1 (41%, p<0.0001), Nup160 (65%, p<0.0001), Nup153 (155%, p = 0.006) and Nup93 (88%, p<0.0001) compared with CNT. However, Nup155 and translocated promoter region (TPR) did not show significant differences in their levels in any etiology. Regarding the distribution of these proteins in cell nucleus, only NDC1 showed differences in HF. In addition, in the pathological group we obtained good relationship between the ventricular function parameters (LVEDD and LVESD) and Nup160 (r = -0382, p = 0.004; r = -0.290, p = 0.033; respectively). Conclusions: This study shows alterations in specific proteins (NDC1, Nup160, Nup153 and Nup93) that compose NPC in ischaemic and dilated human heart. These changes, related to ventricular function, could be accompanied by alterations in the nucleocytoplasmic transport. Therefore, our findings may be the basis for a new approach to HF management.
title: Heart failure induces significant changes in nuclear pore complex of human cardiomyocytes

Key Analyses & Framework Quantum Foundations & Entanglement: The double slit separates coherent alternatives, receiver-defined effects, Born weighting, and the $n = 1$ record. The Sorkin hierarchy and reconstruction literature delimit what is already formally known and leave open the physical motivation for second-order weighting. Entanglement is analyzed through a missing-loss audit: spatial routing, operational differentiation, and dynamical decoupling do not by themselves demonstrate ontological severance of a nonfactorizable joint state. Ontology & Event-Factualization: Primitive factualization is treated as a technical event-ontology posit, with fundamental agency as a stronger interpretive hypothesis (alongside objective stochasticity, Bohmian completion, Everettian branching, and collapse dynamics as comparison classes). A present-state coherence veto prevents absolute factualization while coherence-bearing degrees of freedom remain causally accessible to future interactions in which their phase relation can again matter. Retained factual consequences provide the bridge to physical history, memory, differential persistence, and increasingly organized agency. Downstream Physics & Empirical Testing: Transition and stabilization are treated as relational roles of one field-energy reality rather than new substances. The synthesis incorporates a fully exposed prospective transition-stabilization kill test in a driven liquid-to-vapor system and preserves planetary, gravitational, and spacetime extensions as explicitly conditional research branches. Methodological Stance: No universal master equation is claimed. The program is a structured ontology, audit, and research architecture whose modules must earn mathematical or empirical closure independently. Philosophical Extensions (Dual-Aspect Hypothesis): A further dual-aspect factualist hypothesis, with a panexperiential extension, distinguishes the publicly accessible objective face of factual processes from a minimally subjective first-person-like aspect associated with irreducible factual resolution. This is presented as a stronger ontological interpretation, not as an experimentally established consequence. It does not identify an elementary subjective aspect with a subject, mind, or consciousness. Complex biological agency is treated as potentially nested and hierarchically integrated, while the combination of elementary subjective loci into a unified subject is left as an explicit unresolved problem.

summary: This repository provides the complete replication package for the paper "The Impact of Change Scope on Incremental Software Delivery: A Multi-Host Comparison of Monolithic and Microservice Architectures", accepted for presentation at the Lean and Agile Software Development (LASD) track of the 42nd ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC 2027). The study investigates how the scope of incremental software changes relates to local build-and-redeployment time in monolithic and microservice architectures. Two functionally equivalent applications implemented in Python and FastAPI were evaluated using six change scenarios involving one, two, or three services. The experiment was conducted on two Windows 11 hosts using Docker Desktop and WSL2, producing 240 observations. Repository contents: Complete benchmark source code and Docker Compose configurations. PowerShell scripts for experiment execution. Original measurement datasets from both experimental hosts. Python scripts for statistical analysis and result reproduction. Reproducible figures and descriptive statistics. Additional interaction analysis, bootstrap confidence intervals, and sensitivity checks. Supplementary material documenting the experimental environment, measurement procedure, results, and threats to validity. The repository includes instructions for reproducing the analyses and verifying the reported results. Scope and limitations: The measurements cover local application building and redeployment rather than the complete CI/CD pipeline. The experimental design does not fully separate architectural effects from container-management overhead or scenario-specific characteristics. Additional statistical analyses should therefore be interpreted as exploratory and conditional on the tested scenarios. Version: 1.0.0 License: MIT License.

summary: This repository provides supporting research code for the manuscript "LoRA-Based Diffusion Data Augmentation for Underwater Garbage Detection: An Empirical Study with YOLOv8s", submitted to Scientific Reports. The study investigates whether class-specific Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) provides additional benefits over ControlNet-conditioned synthetic data augmentation for underwater garbage detection using YOLOv8s. The archive includes selected Python source code for paired synthetic-image generation workflows, data and annotation quality assurance, detector-training controls, validation procedures, and exploratory Kernel Inception Distance (KID) analysis. The experiments use a frozen grouped dataset partition with 3,566 training images, 997 validation images, 471 test images, and 96 excluded images. The full-data comparison evaluates real-only training (A), ControlNet-only augmentation (E), and ControlNet-plus-LoRA augmentation (F) using five matched detector seeds. A separate 50%-training-data sensitivity analysis is evaluated on the validation set only. The released archive contains supporting code, configuration information, integrity checksums, and selected aggregate results. Original datasets, model checkpoints, and some historical execution records are not redistributed. Certain historical code versions have unresolved provenance, and the archive does not constitute a fully verified, one-command reproduction of the complete experiments. The experimental findings do not establish a consistent incremental detection benefit from LoRA over matched ControlNet-only augmentation.

summary: NeoN is a next generation implementation of a CFD core. It leverages the features of modern C++ to implement core routines to efficiently solve PDEs required by CFD frameworks like OpenFOAM, and thus helps to catch up with the rapidly evolving HPC ecosystem. Our design goals are: Platform portable for all CPU and GPU hardware vendors Modular design leveraging the existing simulation software ecosystem like Kokkos, sundials, PETSc, or Ginkgo A domain specific language that encodes complex partial differential equations in a concise yet powerful form Simple adoption within OpenFOAM Target multiphysics simulations and enable simple integration of coupling software like preCICE The v0.3 release adds experimental distributed support, so NeoN runs across multiple MPI ranks and GPUs: processor boundaries with exact processor-face geometry, distributed linear system assembly through Ginkgo, mesh partitioning and GPU-aware halo exchange. NeoN is now usable from Python through nanobind bindings, published as pre-built wheels on PyPI ( pip install neon-pde ) and as conda packages for CPU and CUDA on prefix.dev. It also extends the numerics, with slip and inletOutlet boundary conditions, corrected and limited-corrected face-normal gradients, linearUpwind and backward schemes, tensor primitives, and an expression optimizer that fuses DSL operators. The linear algebra layer gains COO and CSR matrices, cell-based assembly, an L1-norm stopping criterion, merged-Pgm multigrid coarsening with setup reuse, and Umpire memory pools. Integration into OpenFOAM applications is demonstrated in our NeoFOAM repository. A full list of changes can be found in the CHANGELOG.md . Thank you to everyone who contributed to NeoN.

summary: Code, data and results for the paper "Do Python Wheels Keep the Promises Their Tags Make? A Verifier and an Audit of the Most Downloaded PyPI Projects". wtv (tool/wtv.py, version 0.1.2) reads a published Python wheel by HTTP range requests, parses every ELF, Mach-O and PE member, and checks nine promises its filename tags make: architecture, the manylinux glibc floor, external libraries, musl, the macOS deployment target, the stable ABI (abi3), the interpreter tag, purity of py*-none-any wheels, and agreement between the filename and the WHEEL file. The package holds the analysis plan written before data collection with its dated change log, the frame of the 2,000 most downloaded PyPI projects, one record per verified wheel (18,102 wheels of the latest stable releases), the comparison with auditwheel 6.8.2 and abi3audit 0.0.26 with every disagreement classified by hand, the precision sample with its evidence and negation control, and every script that produced the reported numbers. The same content is at https://github.com/emilhuseyn/wheel-tag-verifier. Licences: code MIT; data and results CC BY 4.0.

The package holds the analysis plan written before data collection with its dated change log, the frame of the 2,000 most downloaded PyPI projects, one record per verified wheel (18,102 wheels of the latest stable releases), the comparison with auditwheel 6.8.2 and abi3audit 0.0.26 with every disagreement classified by hand, the precision sample with its evidence and negation control, and every script that produced the reported numbers. The same content is at https://github.com/emilhuseyn/wheel-tag-verifier. Licences: code MIT; data and results CC BY 4.0.
title: wtv: wheel tag verifier, and data and replication package for an audit of the most downloaded PyPI projects

summary: Offer-by-offer traces of 1,000 seeded scenarios in which one simulated consumer negotiates price, quantity and delivery time with three simulated manufacturing providers whose preferences, ranges, reservation values and concession behaviour vary. The dataset contains 1,000 sessions, 3,000 negotiations and 26,818 offers. All values are synthetic. The dataset contains no personal data and no data from real companies. The data were generated with a seeded Python script (master seed 2026) that replays the negotiation protocol of the first MaaSAI SPADE agent prototype without a real-time clock or XMPP. The code is included in reproducibility_code_v1.0.0.zip and regenerates the data files byte for byte. Known limitations: the dataset documents a baseline prototype, not the current MaaSAI negotiation strategy. The prototype does not stop a provider from freezing an offer outside its declared ranges: 493 of the 995 agreements are in this situation. They are kept and flagged with final_within_provider_limits = 0. MaaSAI DMP code: MaaSAI_06014_SyntheticNegotiationScenarios_T6.5. Funded by the European Commission under Grant Agreement No. 101177368.

summary: Accurate petroleum inventory reconciliation is a key requirement for the safe and efficient operation of storage terminals. Conventional reconciliation is often performed through periodic reports, manually consolidated measurements, or separate tank and flow-meter records. Such practices can delay the identification of discrepancies and make it difficult to distinguish actual inventory changes from measurement errors, time-alignment problems, and incomplete transfer records. This paper proposes a SCADA-based real-time monitoring architecture that integrates tank level, product temperature, density, flow-meter measurements, historical process data, and tank calibration tables to calculate inventory changes and identify abnormal reconciliation residuals. The proposed system includes data acquisition, signal validation, time synchronization, tank-volume reconstruction, flow accounting, balance calculation, alarm management, and operator visualization. A staged implementation and validation methodology is presented, with emphasis on traceability, measurement uncertainty, and human verification. The framework is a design proposal and has not yet been validated through reported field trials; therefore, no measured improvement in accuracy or loss reduction is claimed.
tags: SCADA; petroleum storage terminal; real-time monitoring; inventory reconciliation; tank gauging; flow measurement; mass balance; measurement uncertainty; alarm management.
title: DEVELOPMENT OF A SCADA-BASED REAL-TIME MONITORING SYSTEM FOR PETROLEUM INVENTORY RECONCILIATION
